extracted.intended_audience: Individual authors (independent writers, researchers, scholars, journalists) seeking NEH Public Scholars grants to write nonfiction books in the humanities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the NEH Public Scholars program, which funds individual authors to research and write well‑researched nonfiction books in the humanities for a broad public. Covers eligibility, topical scope, budget/period rules, application submission, and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output — Books for a broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants support research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to the creation and publication of well‑researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must propose a project that will result in a nonfiction book communicating the significance of humanities research to a broad audience. Sample funded projects are provided as exemplars (e.g., biographies, cultural histories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope — American history/culture and Western civilization (2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Public Scholars competition will only accept projects for research in American history and culture and Western civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive applications must focus on topics in the history, culture, and government of the United States in any period from the Colonial Era to the present, or topics in Western civilization from antiquity to the present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — prior publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have written at least one nonfiction book published by a university or trade press and be credited as its sole author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict eligibility requirement (sole‑author credit). No advanced degree is required; writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant type and payment destination
rubrics_metrics.description: The program accepts individual applicants (writers with or without academic affiliation) and especially encourages independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Scholar awards are paid directly to the applicant, not to their institutions — applicants should plan finances and institutional involvement accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award amount: $60,000 ($5,000 per month). Period of performance: six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project start dates are specified (e.g., April 1, 2027; September 1, 2028 for the cycle shown). Budget and timeline must fit within the six‑to‑twelve‑month term and monthly payment cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: One‑application‑per‑deadline rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply to only one NEH program at each deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who submit to this program may not submit to another NEH program with the same deadline; verify program selection before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may support research, writing, travel, and other activities that lead to the creation and publication of the proposed book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should budget for these activities and justify expenses in the application following the Notice of Funding Opportunity instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application narrative length and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Application narratives may only be three pages long (current Notice of Funding Opportunity page limits and formatting requirements apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample application narratives on the site may not comply with current page limits — applicants must follow the rules in the current Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and submission procedures (Grants.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register for a Grants.gov account, add an 'individual applicant' profile, and submit the application package on Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Grants.gov instructions for account setup and profile management (My Account → Manage Profiles → Add Profile). Download Adobe Reader and follow tips for making PDFs. After submission, monitor and verify confirmation e‑mails from Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation — submission and applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program staff will request letters of reference from recommenders on or about three to four weeks after the deadline; applicants will be notified by e‑mail when each letter has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the fifth Grants.gov confirmation message, applicants may check the status of letters in the secure area of NEH’s website using their NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number. Applicants are responsible for ensuring recommenders received solicitation links and for sending reminders if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on Use of Artificial Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should consult NEH’s Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals as part of program resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow any restrictions or disclosure requirements in the NEH AI policy when preparing proposal narratives or other application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to read Notice of Funding Opportunity and Program Announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must read the Notice of Funding Opportunity and the Program Announcement for Public Scholars to understand all expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and to prepare an effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents contain the definitive instructions, eligibility details, page limits, and other requirements; applicants should not rely solely on summary webpages or sample narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirming submission and tracking statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting the application, Grants.gov will send up to five e‑mail messages confirming receipt at different stages; applicants should verify they have received all confirmation messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email filters may send messages to spam/junk folders; applicants should monitor e‑mail and the NEH secure status page to ensure the application and letters are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project framing — communicate scholarly significance to broad audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive applications should strengthen the research underlying books and communicate the significance of their research to the broadest possible range of readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program encourages academic writers to adapt scholarship for public audiences and non‑academic writers to deepen their humanities research; proposals should demonstrate how the project will reach and engage general readers.
